description: Core concepts in microeconomics and macroeconomics

basic_concepts.scarcity: Resources are limited; desires are unlimited; necessitates choices
basic_concepts.opportunity_cost: The value of the next best alternative forgone when making a choice
basic_concepts.trade_off: Gaining something requires giving up something else
basic_concepts.marginal_thinking: Decisions made at the margin; what is the next unit worth?
basic_concepts.incentives: People respond to incentives; good policy aligns incentives with desired outcomes

supply_demand.law_of_demand: As price increases, quantity demanded decreases (inverse relationship)
supply_demand.law_of_supply: As price increases, quantity supplied increases (direct relationship)
supply_demand.equilibrium: Price where quantity supplied equals quantity demanded
supply_demand.surplus: Quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded; price falls
supply_demand.shortage: Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied; price rises

elasticity.price_elasticity_demand: % change in quantity demanded / % change in price
elasticity.elastic: Elasticity > 1; demand changes more than price
elasticity.inelastic: Elasticity < 1; demand changes less than price (e.g., insulin, gasoline)

market_structures.perfect_competition: Many sellers, homogeneous products, price takers; agricultural commodities
market_structures.monopoly: Single seller; price maker; high barriers to entry
market_structures.oligopoly: Few dominant firms; strategic interdependence; OPEC, airlines
market_structures.monopolistic: Many firms, differentiated products; restaurants, clothing

market_failures.externalities: Costs or benefits to third parties not in the transaction (pollution, education)
market_failures.public_goods: Non-excludable, non-rival; government must provide (national defense, lighthouses)
market_failures.information_asymmetry: One party has more information than another (used car market, insurance)
market_failures.market_power: Monopolies can restrict output and raise prices inefficiently

gdp.definition: Gross Domestic Product; total value of goods and services produced in a country
gdp.components: GDP = C + I + G + (X - M); Consumption + Investment + Government + Net Exports
gdp.per_capita: GDP divided by population; measure of living standards

inflation.definition: General increase in price level over time
inflation.cpi: Consumer Price Index; measures inflation by tracking basket of goods

types.frictional: Between jobs; voluntary; inevitable and healthy
types.cyclical: Due to economic downturns; targeted by policy

unemployment.natural_rate: Unemployment when economy at full employment (~4–5%)

macroeconomics.fiscal_policy: Government spending and taxation to influence economy
macroeconomics.monetary_policy: Central bank control of money supply and interest rates

schools_of_thought.classical: Markets self-correct; minimal government intervention; Smith, Ricardo
schools_of_thought.keynesian: Government spending needed to stabilize economy; aggregate demand matters; Keynes
schools_of_thought.monetarist: Control money supply; inflation is monetary phenomenon; Friedman
schools_of_thought.behavioral: People are not fully rational; cognitive biases affect economic decisions; Thaler, Kahneman

international_trade.comparative_advantage: Country should produce what it does at lowest opportunity cost; Ricardo
international_trade.terms_of_trade: Ratio of export prices to import prices
international_trade.wto: World Trade Organization; 164 members; dispute resolution; reduces trade barriers
